analysis.description: The paper investigates the development of a set of independent policies that can address various downstream reinforcement learning tasks using generalized policy evaluation and improvement. It proposes an algorithm for constructing a behavior basis that ensures good performance across tasks and validates these results with empirical tests.

type.justification: The paper primarily focuses on proving theoretical properties related to constructing policy sets in reinforcement learning contexts and validates these concepts with experimental results.
type.quote: We show theoretically that, under certain assumptions, having access to a specific set of diverse policies, which we call a set of independent policies, can allow for instantaneously achieving high-level performance on all possible downstream tasks.

name.justification: The primary research field is reinforcement learning, as the paper specifically discusses constructing a set of policies to perform well on reinforcement learning tasks.
name.quote: Reinforcement learning (RL) studies the problem of building rational decision-making agents that maximize long term cumulative reward through trial-and-error interaction with a given environment.

name.justification: The paper addresses the problem of transferring knowledge across multiple reinforcement learning tasks using a set of learned policies.
name.quote: We study the problem of learning a good set of policies, so that when combined together, they can solve a wide variety of unseen reinforcement learning tasks with no or very little new data.
